what: A census of every block TYPE present in stored page documents in production, per store. Types only — no tenant copy, no props, no ids. The guard (scripts/check-stored-blocks.test.ts) asserts every type recorded here resolves in the live block registry (lib/page-editor/config.tsx), so retiring a block that stored data still names fails CI instead of silently blanking a section on someone's page.
why: ADR-978 stopped an unknown type from DESTROYING a document, but nothing noticed that five types were already orphaned — they were found by hand, twice (ADR-977 D-9, then again for LIVE-028). A fail-safe with no gate that notices it fired is an invisible regression (AGENTS.md, Deploy safety).
howToRecapture: Run the SQL in `recaptureQuery` against production (read-only) and rewrite `stores` from the result, then set `capturedAt`. Re-capture after applying a document migration; the guard reads the registry live, so it does NOT need a re-capture when the registry changes.
scope: The Puck-shaped registry only (lib/page-editor/config.tsx). The Spotlight union (lib/spotlight/blocks/schema.ts) and the entity-block registry (lib/entity-blocks/registry.ts) are separate catalogs with separate storage and are NOT covered here.
recaptureQuery: with docs as (select 'pages.data' as store, slug as doc_key, data as doc from pages where data is not null union all select 'pages.published_data', slug, published_data from pages where published_data is not null union all select 'spaces.preferences.puck', slug, preferences->'puck' from spaces where preferences ? 'puck' union all select 'spaces.preferences.pageDocs', s.slug||'#'||d.key, d.value from spaces s, lateral jsonb_each(coalesce(s.preferences->'pageDocs','{}'::jsonb)) d), items as (select store, doc_key, e->>'type' as type from docs, lateral jsonb_array_elements(doc->'content') e where jsonb_typeof(doc->'content')='array') select store, type, count(*) as blocks, count(distinct doc_key) as docs from items group by store, type order by store, type;

stores.note: The marketing draft documents. The five orphan types were rewritten to their registry successors by 20270305000000 (LIVE-028); every type below resolves.
Clean before and after the LIVE-028 rewrite, which deliberately did not touch it.
18 Space documents, 12 distinct types, all resolving.

quarantineRule: A type may appear here ONLY while a migration that retires it is in the tree. The guard READS that SQL and confirms it maps this exact type to this exact successor — existing is not enough — so a quarantine entry cannot outlive its fix. It also fails if the registry has since started resolving the type, or if the successor does not resolve. The list may only shrink: it empties when the owner promotes and applies the migration and re-captures the census. There is no line-level escape hatch — losing a tenant's authored block is not something a comment may authorise.
whyTheMigrationIsNotInSupabaseMigrations: A file in supabase/migrations/ IS an assertion that production has run it, and CI arms check:migrations rule 4 (ADR-1007) with real credentials — so an unapplied file there fails the build. ✅ NOTHING IS STAGED TODAY: `quarantine` is empty. This field used to instruct the next author to stage SQL in docs/proposals/ with a promotion banner; that directory was deleted in #2153 when its last occupant was promoted into supabase/migrations/. If a future entry needs staging, pick a home that exists and record it here in the same change.
